--- Page 654 ---
<meta>This page continues the editorial introduction regarding the sources and choices made for this edition of the Bible. It concludes the sentence from the previous page concerning the translations of Nerses of Lambron.</meta>

...translations by Nerses of Lambron <note>Nerses of Lambron (1153–1198) was a famous Archbishop of Tarsus and a prolific scholar known for his translations and theological works.</note>. It is a great wonder how both the original Greek source text and the preceding ones disappeared from among us, which is why these were not known to European bibliographers.

Furthermore, regarding the prefaces and the lists for the Acts and the Epistles of the Apostles included here—all of which were, as is believed, the work of Euthalius <note>Euthalius was a 5th-century deacon credited with developing a system of chapters and summaries for the New Testament to make it easier to study.</note>—we have omitted the full table of contents or the indices of lections and citations due to their extreme length. Instead, we decided to supplement this volume with that exhortatory text entitled the **Supplication of Euthalius**, which all manuscripts, including our own exemplar, append to the end of the Catholic Epistles <note>The "Catholic" or "Universal" Epistles include the letters of James, Peter, John, and Jude.</note>. This particular writing was so highly esteemed and frequently used among us that it even became a common custom to include it among the Lectionary <note>original: "Chashots" — the liturgical book containing the scripture readings for the Eucharist.</note> readings of the Liturgy at the conclusion of the Epistle of Jude, which is performed on the Saturday preceding Pentecost. This can be seen in manuscript Lectionaries and Directories of Feasts <note>original: "Tonatsuyts" — the liturgical calendar or "Directorium" that dictates which hymns and readings are used each day.</note>. It seems it was even more thoughtlessly moved by later scribes to the actual day of Pentecost itself, as if it were a reading to follow the Acts of the Apostles, which is how modern printed Lectionaries and Directories of Feasts have it today.

In the present additions, we might have also included the *Death of the Prophets*, which our manuscripts contained at the end of each of their respective prophecies, along with certain other writings. We omitted these from the current order, as we did with the *Testament of the Twelve Patriarchs* <note>An apocryphal text presenting the final words of the twelve sons of Jacob.</note> together with the separate story of *Joseph the Beautiful*, which were found in two of the aforementioned manuscripts. However, the excessive length of this volume, as we have said, leads us to leave those for a more suitable occasion to be published as a separate edition. By doing this, we are not guaranteeing their authenticity, but rather providing a resource for our scholars who wish to research ancient literature.

But know this: that for both of them — for these and for those — a reckoning awaits before God. <note>The Armenian text emphasizes divine justice as the ultimate equalizer between rich and poor, despite the obvious social injustice described throughout this passage.</note> \* For the great man, goodness is praiseworthy where there is no sin; but poverty is wicked in the mouths of the ungodly. \* Whether evil or good, \* a person's face reveals what is joyful and what is sorrowful within them.

## CHAPTER 22

<margin>1</margin> A lazy man is compared to a stone covered in filth; everyone hisses <margin>2</margin> at his disgrace. * A lazy man is like a lump of dung; whoever picks it up <margin>3</margin> shakes it off his hands. * A father is shamed by an uninstructed child, and <margin>4</margin> the birth of a daughter is a loss. <note>This reflects the ancient Near Eastern context where daughters were often viewed through the lens of dowry costs and social standing.</note> * An impudent woman brings shame upon both <margin>5</margin> her father and her husband. * Music during a time of mourning is like a tale told at <margin>6</margin> the wrong time; but wisdom and instruction are always timely for the wise. <margin>7</margin> * He who teaches a fool is like one who glues together a broken pot, <margin>8</margin> * or like one who tells a story to someone who will not listen; he is like one who <margin>9</margin> wakes a sleeper from a deep sleep. * He who recounts wisdom to a fool—and <margin>10</margin> asks for a word from him—the fool says, "What are you?" or "What did you say?" <margin>11</margin> * Weep for the dead, for the light has left him; and weep for the <term>fool</term> <note>original: "մորոսի" (morosi) — derived from the Greek 'mōros', meaning a dullard or a fool.</note> <margin>12</margin> for wisdom has left him. * Weep only a little for the dead, for he is at <margin>13</margin> rest; but the life of a fool is worse than death. * Mourning for the dead lasts <margin>14</margin> seven days, but for the ungodly and the fool, it lasts all the days of his life. <margin>15</margin> * Do not speak much with a fool, and do not travel with the senseless. <margin>16</margin> * Turn away from him and you will find rest; otherwise, you will be defiled by <margin>17</margin> his death <note>likely referring to the fool's moral decay or "dead" character</note>, or he will be a burden upon your blood. * What is heavier than <margin>18</margin> lead? ---

# THE WORDS OF SIRACH:

An obedient mind and a temperate throat are the glory of a man; but the greedy are like a **leaking vessel** that can never be filled. An envious man shall be burned by his own thoughts; but the simple-minded <note>In this context, meaning the pure or sincere of heart.</note> are like the **myrtle tree**, which is green at all times. The wedding and the joy of the envious and the hypocrite shall turn to weeping for him. Whenever an evil man and a hypocrite eats honey, he shall receive a taste of bitterness. Wicked men waste away and melt within their own thoughts. A man who is needy and miserly, even if he possesses many treasures and precious stones, such a man is **poor**; and from his possessions, not even a single bristle <note>original: "խոզան" (bristle/stubble), implying the smallest, most worthless portion.</note> shall reach him as a provision, and he shall be tossed about in vain like the waves of the sea. But for the **generous**, those who speak their praise are more numerous than the sands of the sea, and their hearts shall not be saddened. But as for those who spend wastefully and are generous toward harlots, they shall quickly...

<header>WORDS</header>

...in the [right] season. For the expense of one at a fitting time has the comfort of warm **gold**; but he who spends aimlessly, even a lead coin shall be counted as but one of copper. You do not see the faces of people-pleasers and hypocrites blushing <note>original: "կարմրացել" (reddened/blushing), implying a lack of healthy shame or genuine emotion.</note>, but rather they have become like **sun-scorched greens**.

The strength of giants and wrestlers is great, but those who restrain their own anger and desire, and fight within their own minds—that is severe power and **strength**. Those who are poor in possessions are despised by their servants and handmaidens, and they receive no honor in the marketplaces, nor are they glorified at the gates of kings.

A foolish daughter causes her father to be dragged away, dishonored, and killed. But a **modest** one is better than seven sons. A cruel and impious man is not humbled even when he sees his companion dead. Licentious lips and a proud tongue do not know the path of **peace** and **righteousness**. A gentle tongue and sweet lips hold the place of great gifts.

A secret fallen into a glutton is like fire in linen. He who does evil with laughter is like a mockingly broken liver <note>An idiom suggesting a person whose internal character is shattered or someone acting with insane, self-destructive mirth.</note>. The impious man is like vinegar that makes food bitter and harms the stomach; so too are the evils of the man who is led by them. No one rejoices at a man's death, except for the plunderer for whom there is great joy.

If you place a deposit <note>original: "աւանդ" (a trust, pledge, or deposit of money).</note>, it becomes a tool for the righteous, but a snare for the sinner, who shall be caught by his own hands. Sin and righteousness cannot be worked together like silver mixed with copper; they are as foreign to each other as fire and wood. The coward will not complete the work of war; but the brave man, though he loves peace, does not grow weak.

Anger corrupts precious beauty. The lustful man is like one lulled to sleep by wolves. They said the root of instruction is bitter, but its fruit is sweet; but if you wish to be **wise**, know the time. Those who consider an oath to be a bridge shall sink into firm depths; and woe to those who cross by that bridge!

Wherever a God-loving and just man turns, a sweet sun shall rise from his face. Woe to those who follow after vanity, for it is like a man's shadow; and he who goes against the desires of his soul gives a ransom for his soul. (From injury to the **tongue**, the head is broken, and the jaws are crushed.)

To the senseless, iron and copper seem like choice gold; and those who please themselves shall often be put to shame. A rebuking and corroded tongue causes the abundance of hands to be despised; but truthful tongues are not abandoned in the marketplaces. If you pay attention to the face of a false witness...

<page-num>39</page-num>
<header>SIRACH</header>

...reveal <note>The word completes a verb from the previous page, likely "reveal" or "disclose."</note> it: it is an obvious lie. If you enter a church, the tongue of a carrion-eating dog and the lying tongue of a dog in the marketplaces [should be far from you]. He who is **wise** is an unbreakable seal. The deceitful man, even if he be a freeman, is like the son of a harlot <note>original: "պոռնկորդի" (pornkorid); in this context, it suggests that deceit strips a person of their noble or legitimate standing.</note>. A sincere servant is a **priceless** freeman. The south wind shall not come to the deceitful man in the spring. A vengeful man is like fire—a temple of wrath. A disobedient son makes a father love the son of a handmaid <note>A warning that a biological heir can lose their father's affection to a servant's child through poor behavior.</note>. The sons of deceitful men, even if they appear sincere, shall not inherit goodness. 

He who sits with the wise is praised by the wise; but he who associates with the foolish will easily become a fool. He who allows his son to go according to his own whims, he truly hates him. The **righteous** shrink from the house of the lawless and do not satisfy their hunger there; but the lawless shall be satiated in the house of sinners. A road that seems straight to one, but is crooked to many—woe to him who travels upon it. If someone laughs audaciously, let him leave some room for weeping. Everyone deceives a simple-minded man. 

As you seek firm scales for your chests of treasure, seek also the peace of your confidant, and honor him. Deadly sins are removed by skilled physicians, but the souls of those who take bribes shall be incurable. As a deer melts <note>original: "հալի" (melts/vanishes); describing the prey's terror and disappearance before a predator.</note> before a lion, so do sins before **mercy**. He who strikes his companion with his foot, let him not forget the return of his repayment. 

Do not increase your enmity toward your enemy, but leave room for his friendship. Do not open all the treasures of your thoughts to your beloved and your friend. There is great readiness in the marketplace for a silent man; everyone listens together when he speaks. For if speaking is considered **silver**, remaining silent is **gold**. One should not frequent a house of ill-repute <note>original: "քողանոց" (k'oghanots), literally a place of veils or masks, referring to a brothel.</note>. A foolish and impious man does not cease to find excuses against God. A wise enemy is better than a foolish loved one. 

If a shadow could be touched, or the sun could be grasped, then also would penance for past deeds be of use <note>This suggests that once an act is done, mere regret without a change in nature is as impossible as grasping the sun.</note>. He who rebels against the house of God—He who knows him shall raise against him a smiter who does not know the Lord God. Drunken loved ones are unstable enemies, scattered by many conflicting counsels. Do not frequently warn a king, lest he suspect evil from you. 

A man of bad news and mourning flees from a village that is at the crossroads; but he who is generous welcomes guests not only with bread, but with sweet words. A sharp tongue serves a man as long as it is **silent**; but when you speak inappropriately, you become its servant. The tongue is a domestic beast in a man's mouth; but when he lets it loose, it eats him. A thousand words of a foolish man produce no results.

<header>EZRA</header>

...half a word; but the wise man’s half-word binds a thousand words. Just as traps are set for horses at their flanks, so it does not benefit a man if he is greedy for a woman's tongue and behaves foolishly. If you wish to recognize the self-pleasing and the foolish, know them by this: they are quick to anger, they give gifts where they are not deserved, they do not distinguish an enemy from a loved one, they do not keep secrets in their heart, they speak too much at improper times, and they trust every man. 

My child, two things follow the dead to the grave: those who remain and the survivors. But that which enters with him stays with him: his deeds, whether good or evil. The other two return to their own places, and the deceased gains nothing from them. 

A man is like a tree: just as water benefits a tree, so prayer benefits a person’s soul. As branches are the glory of a tree, so fasting is the glory of a person. As green leaves are the splendor of trees, so the love of the poor <note>original: "աղքատասիրութի" (aghkatasirut'i); this refers to the virtue of charity or almsgiving.</note> is the splendor of a man. Now, if one of these is missing, the tree cannot take root; likewise, if a man does not do these things, he cannot be called a "perfect man." It is not right for a man of counsel—who carries authority and needs upon his shoulders—to sleep through the entire night.

# EZRA THE THIRD

<margin>CH. 1</margin> <margin>1</margin> **I**, Salathiel—who am also called Ezra— <margin>2</margin> was in Babylon in the thirtieth year. I was lying on my bed, and I was thinking about the ruin of Zion and the prosperity of Babylon. <margin>3</margin> My spirit was overwhelmed, <margin>4</margin> and I began to speak words of awe to the Most High. And I said: "O Lord my God, you created the heavens and the earth and everything that is in them. <margin>5</margin> And after that, you created man with your incorruptible hands and breathed into him the breath of life, and he stood before you. <margin>6</margin> You placed him in the Garden of Delights <note>This refers to Paradise or the Garden of Eden.</note> which your right hand had planted. <margin>7</margin> You gave him a commandment so that they might know they are your handiwork. But he transgressed it and was deceived. Because of this, you justly and immediately decreed death for him and for all the generations that came from him, <margin>8</margin> who also transgressed the commands of your holy laws..."

### Chapter 4
<margin>1</margin> And after I had thought upon this, an angel was sent to me, <margin>2</margin> whose name was the holy <gloss>holy</gloss> Uriel. ✱ He began to speak with me and said, "Your heart is distraught in this life, in your desire to comprehend the way of the Most High."

8 ✱ I spoke of both, for they had thought a vain thought; for the earth was given to the forests, but the sand <note>original: "աւազոյն"</note> of the sea to hold back the waves. ✱ And he said to me: You have judged rightly; why then have you not judged concerning the things spoken to you? ✱ Just as the earth was given to the forests, and the place of the sand to the waves, so also those who dwell upon the earth are allowed to understand earthly things, and those who dwell in the heavens can recognize heavenly things.

### THIRD

...friends against acquaintances, nation against nation, people against people, and priests against priests. Or practiced righteousness, or hated lawlessness, or sided with truth, or showed mercy, or hated plunder, or sought the Most High with all his heart, or did anyone love his neighbor with holiness?"

It shall give answer and say, "No such person is found with me." ✱ In those times, men shall expect to receive something from the Most High; they shall seek and shall not receive. They shall labor with toil and not find rest. They shall eat and not enjoy the works of their hands. They shall walk, and their ways shall not be straight. They shall be overtaken at the end of the times. 

In pains and in sorrow and in sighing—for they not only changed the laws, but also rejected the Most High himself upon the earth, as much as was in them. For this reason, the sword shall come upon them, and the Most High shall reign in the seat of judgment, and he shall come and change them. And the Most High shall show his glory in him. Then he shall repay them with torments, as they thought in their pride, and he shall despise them likewise.

✱ These signs I was commanded to tell you. If again, once more, you seek the Most High with fasting and tears for seven days, you shall hear things even greater than these. 

✱ And when I awoke and had heard this, I kept it in mind. And from fear, the appearance of my body was marred, and my strength departed from me, and my soul drew near to fainting. But I pondered in my mind that no one of us can survive, and we die like the beasts, in whom there is no wisdom, and who are tortured in eternal torments. Deeply pondering this, I was troubled. ✱ The Angel Uriel came again and strengthened me, and set me firm upon my feet, and said to me: "Do not be sorrowful, for you were shown before the time what the Most High is to do in the final days. You have found grace with God." <note>original: "յԱյ" — an abbreviation for "յԱստուծոյ" (from God).</note>

✱ And after this, Phanuel <note>original: "Փանուէլ". In other versions of this text, this figure is often named Phaltiel or Salathiel.</note> came to me, who was the leader of the people, and said to me: "Why has the color of your face become so unsightly? ✱ Do you not know what has been entrusted to you in this world of our pilgrimage?"

<summary>The Archangel Uriel describes the total moral and social collapse of the end times, where the earth itself testifies that no righteous person remains. Ezra is physically overwhelmed by the vision but is strengthened by Uriel and questioned by the leader Phanuel.</summary>

For the way of the Most High is incomprehensible. # THIRD [BOOK OF EZRA]

...very deep water, * and only one path passes between the fire and the water; there is no place for anyone else to be, except only for the measure of a man’s foot. * And if no one desires to inherit it, he must first pass through the narrow [way]; otherwise, he cannot receive the inheritance. * And I said, "It is so." And he answered and said to me: In the same way, a portion of inheritance is given to Israel <note>original: "Իլի" (Ili) — a common abbreviation in Armenian manuscripts for "Israyeli" (Israel).</note>. * For the sake of mankind, God made this world and filled it with all goodness. And He gave them laws <note>original: "օրէնս" (ōrens) — referring specifically to the Mosaic Law or divine decrees.</note>, so that by them they might conduct themselves and reign in a kingdom that is good, sober, and blameless.

But they did not keep them; instead, they rejected Him. And the Most High <term>Barjryaln</term> <note>The standard Armenian title for God as the "Most High."</note> determined in His mind to reject those who rebelled against Him. For this reason, the entrances of this world are harsh and difficult and full of suffering. * For unless they first enter the narrow and thin path of this world, * and unless those who have entered endure with patience, they shall not receive the good things prepared [for them] which existed before the world was. * But you are confused because you are mortal. * And do not be troubled because you are corruptible, but look to what is near, and fix in your mind what is to happen in the future.

And I said: "Then it is the righteous who inherit the good things; and they consider it well to enter through the narrow and thin path. * But those who are weak and do not pass through their holiness, even though they knew the trial of affliction, have distanced themselves from the eternal goods."

And he said to me: "And I say to you, you are not better than the Most High, nor more sweet than God, nor more a lover of mankind than He. * All who transgress the commandment of the Lord shall perish, rather than the laws being despised. * God strictly commanded mankind what they should do to live, and what they should keep so as not to be tormented. * But they refused everything. And against the Holy God they said that He is not the Most High, and that there is no reward for good or evil deeds. They perverted their own ways, * and they rejected His laws, and they despised His will, and they denied His covenants. They lacked faith in His holy ones, and they [disregarded] His chosen ones. * And for this reason, listen, brother: vanity of vanities for the vain, and fullness for the full. * Behold, the time shall come when the sign that was told to you before shall occur. The city that is now not seen shall be revealed, and every knee of every land shall mourn. * And everyone who remains blameless shall see the glory of the Most High. * Then the Anointed One <term>Odyaln</term> <note>The Armenian term for "Messiah" or "Christ," literally "The Anointed."</note> shall appear openly to men, and He shall make joyful those who remain in faith and patience. * And all those who are buried in the earth shall rise at the voice of the Lord. * And they shall stand..."

# THIRD

...we walked the paths of destruction and the tracks of death, and we departed from the truth of life. He answered and said to me: "You said that the righteous are few and the impious are many; now, hear this: If you possessed precious stones, surely you would prepare everything according to their worthiness; would you consider that which is unworthy to be equal to them? Or would you treat them as if they were lead, or pottery, or something else similar?" 

And I said, "No." 

And he said to me: "Speak to the earth [and ask]: 'Why do you produce so much clay for pottery, but do not bring forth gold in the same way?' And it shall give you an answer and say: 'Because clay is more abundant than iron, and iron than lead, and lead than copper, and copper than silver, and silver than gold, and gold than precious stones.' Choose now, and see which is precious and desirable." 

And I said, "Who does not know that the few and the scarce are what is desirable?" 

And he said to me: "Just as the scarce seems precious and desirable to humans, so too are the few righteous precious to the <term>Most High</term> <note>Armenian: "Barjryaln." The standard title for God in this text, emphasizing His sovereignty over all creation.</note>. And He rejoices over the few who glorified His name on earth, and through whom His name is blessed and praised; for this reason, the righteous shall flourish and be glorified before God. But the lawless multitude shall be like a whirlwind <note>original: "մրրկի նմանեսցէ" — a common biblical metaphor for the sudden and total disappearance of the wicked at the time of judgment.</note>, and they are prepared for the blazing fire; their faces shall be in shame and disgrace." 

And while he was speaking this with me, I sighed from my soul and was troubled, and my spirit grew faint within me, and I said: "O earth, why did you give birth to man, so that he was delivered to eternal torments? For this reason, the human race shall mourn, but the wild beast shall rejoice; and all the <term>offspring of rational beings</term> <note>Armenian: "ծնունդք բանաւորաց." This refers specifically to humans, distinguished from animals by their "logos" or reason.</note> shall lament, but all the four-footed beasts shall be glad. It is much better for them than for us, for they do not expect a resurrection, nor do they await judgments. What benefit is it to us if we enter into judgment and into unceasing torments? It would be better if there were no resurrection for us, so that we might be saved from eternal torments." 

And while I was considering this, he said to me: "From the beginning of creation, before man came to be upon the face of the earth, the Most High prepared beforehand the place of delight and the place of torments. Understand then, that they had laws by which they could have lived, and they did not keep them, but despised them; what punishment shall they have to give on the day of the end? For the Most High was long-suffering <note>A reference to God's patience, allowing time for repentance before the final judgment.</note> for so much time, and they, by despising [the law], destroyed their own souls." 

I gave an answer and said to the angel of the Lord: "I beseech you, Lord, tell me, if after death, when each [soul] is required from us...

**The first path:** that which with much labor strove against all sin.
**The second path:** seeing the prepared torments for the sinners. 
**The third path:** the testimony which God witnesses for it, that with great faith it kept the laws which were given to it. 
**The fourth path:** in which the prepared good things are revealed to it, how it is kept like the angels in great peace and served. 
**The fifth path:** it is glorified with joy, for it has cast off corruption, and from then on it is counted with the angels to inherit the unending light. 
**The sixth path:** in which it is shown how its face shall shine like the sun, and thereafter it shall not be darkened by corruption. 
**The seventh path:** which is higher than all paths, in which it boasts with confidence and boldness, not being ashamed or abashed, but rejoicing, it hastens to see the face of God, whom it served blamelessly in life, by whom it is to be glorified, and from whom it is to receive the reward of compensation. These are the paths of the souls of the righteous.

But the souls of the impious, and those who did not keep the commandment of the Most High and despised His laws, and loathed His servants—they shall not enter into the place of rest forever. Instead, immediately when the souls are separated from the body, they shall enter into eternal torments with sorrow and grief through seven paths.

...in its own time, the womb, <margin>10</margin> which He commanded to give birth, to suckle milk until a certain time; and <margin>11</margin> after that, it is fitting for Him, in His wisdom, to nourish it with the fruits of His own harvest. <margin>12</margin> And He instructs it by His own examples, and little by little causes wisdom and the knowledge of all evil and good to grow within it, and those things which are not so. <margin>13</margin> And after all these years, He causes it to die. <margin>15</margin> And while I was thinking on these things, I opened my mouth and began to entreat the Most High, saying: "O Lord God, as God, have mercy upon Your works and upon Your creatures. Look upon us, and take account of us and our transgressions; <margin>18</margin> for I have heard of the great severity <note>original: "զանխնայութի" — literally "unsparingness," referring to the lack of mercy in the coming judgment.</note> which is to come in the future. <margin>19</margin> Therefore, O Creator of all, long-suffering Most High, hear my voice and give ear to my words which I speak before You, while I stand in prayer before You."

### The Prayer of the Prophet Ezra

You who dwell forever, whose eyes <margin>20</margin> see and examine everything with certainty, and whose upper chambers are in the air; <margin>21</margin> whose throne is inexpressible and whose glory is beyond telling, around whom stand the multitudes of the angelic hosts, serving with fear; <margin>22</margin> and by His command and word He turns spirits into fire <note>A reference to Psalm 104:4, "Who makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire."</note>; <margin>23</margin> whose word is immovable and powerful, who arranges everything according to its proper order; whose command is severe and whose order is awesome; whose look dries up the abysses, and whose word of threat cleaves the earth; who creates everything He wills from nothing, and changes what exists by His power; whose truth bears witness.

<margin>24</margin> Hear the voice of Your servant, and give ear to the requests of Your minister; listen to my words. <margin>25</margin> While I am alive, I will speak. <margin>26</margin> Do not look upon the downfall <note>original: "գլորումն" — literally a "tumbling" or "stumbling," referring to human sin.</note> [of those who] have the will to keep Your commands but are overcome by the thoughts of the evil one. Rather, have mercy like a benefactor and savior, and spare and strengthen us like a healer. For You alone are without sin. Now I beg of you, do not look upon the transgressions of Your people, but upon those who served You uprightly in truth. <margin>27</margin> Spare them; do not repay according to...

<summary>Ezra argues that God’s long labor in creating and nurturing humanity would be in vain if He simply destroyed them, leading into a poetic prayer (the Confessio Ezrae) praising God's sovereignty while pleading for mercy for Israel.</summary>

...their lawless deeds; but because of those who with fear kept Your covenants, spare them. And do not take into account those who walked in wickedness before You; but remember those who willingly acknowledged the fear of You. And do not desire to destroy those who likened their lives to the beasts <note>original: "զվարսն իւրեանց անասնոց նմանեցուցին" — a reference to living purely physical, unspiritual lives without moral law.</note>, but look with compassion upon Your servants who have hoped in Your glory. For we, and those who were before us, have committed deeds worthy of death; but You, O Lord, who are called the **Lover of Mankind** <term>Mardaser: A standard Armenian title for God, equivalent to the Greek "Philanthropos," emphasizing God's inherent affection for humanity</term>, were called long-suffering for the sake of us sinners.

For although we were not of such good works, and did nothing according to Your will, but followed after the impurity of the flesh, You know how to have mercy. Then You shall be called merciful, since those who performed holiness by Your holy will have no need of mercy; for they have the reward of their own deeds in repayment. What are we men, that You should be angry with us in truth? There is no one born upon the earth who has not sinned. In this shall Your compassion be known, when You have mercy and pardon us; and You shall forgive our impiety—we who do not have the substance of good works.

The Lord answered me and said to me: "If sinners return to me with all their heart, I will not think to repay them according to their former sins. But at the departure of their souls, I will judge them as they are <note>This implies a judgment based on the state of the soul at the moment of death rather than a tally of past sins.</note>; and so I will rejoice over those who turn to good works, just as I rejoice over my righteous ones. 

Liken me to a simple farmer; just as a farmer plows and plants as much as he wishes and desires, and at each season takes care of each thing as is necessary. Although it may happen that some of them grow weak and approach decay, he provides care for them in due time; and if the care prevails, he rejoices with great joy, because that which was about to fail grew strong. But if the care is of no use at the proper time, the care shall be put away in sorrow. So shall it be upon the earth: the Most High shall be long-suffering over them. For if they repent according to that which was ordained for them, they have done good; but if not, they shall be punished."

I answered and said: "Since You have permitted me once to speak before You, I beseech You, tell me, Your servant: if the seeds of the farmer do not receive rain in proper measure, they wither; and likewise the man to whom You do not show mercy cannot live. Therefore, spare Your people, Lord, and have mercy on Your inheritance; You shall have mercy on Your possessions and the works of Your hands."

He answered and said to me: "With wretchedness shall those men who dwell in this world become wretched, because... <note>The text cuts off here. The catchword "ամ" suggests the next page begins with "ամբարշտութեամբ" (wickedness) or "ամենայն" (all).</note>

<summary>Ezra pleads for divine mercy for sinners, arguing that God's reputation as "Merciful" is only proven by forgiving the unworthy. God responds with a parable of a farmer, explaining that while He is long-suffering, judgment depends on the soul's final state and its response to His care.</summary>

# EZRA #

...before the powerful judge, and those lives which are not yet seen shall arrive. <margin>34</margin> And corruption shall pass away, and mercy shall cease, and compassion shall be idle; the gates of repentance shall be closed, and long-suffering shall be withdrawn into itself, but faith shall show its fruit. <margin>35</margin> And after one's deeds, the reward and righteousness shall bloom. And then the place of rest for the saints shall appear, and the true paradise of delight; and standing opposite them shall be the furnace of fire and eternal torments, and the **immortal worm** <note>original: "որդն անմահ" — a biblical image for eternal suffering where the conscience or the 'worm' of decay never dies; see Mark 9:48.</note>, which is prepared for the ungodly and the lawless.

And then the Most High shall say to the righteous: "See the place of your rest which was prepared for you from the beginning of creation; enter now and rest, and skip like calves released from the yoke." <note>original: "իբրև զորթս արձակեալ 'ի կապոյ" — a reference to Malachi 4:2, symbolizing the joy of liberation from the burdens of the world.</note> And He shall say to the ungodly and the lawless: "See and know Me, whom you did not serve, or whom you denied, or whose laws you despised. Look at what lies before you: the delight prepared for the righteous, and for you ungodly ones, the fire and eternal torments."

And the **Day of Judgment** <term>Datastan: The final, definitive legal and spiritual accounting of a soul's life</term> shall be like this: no sun shall stand as a light-giver, nor the moon, nor the stars shining; there shall be no shading clouds, nor thunder signaling the passing of seasons, nor cooling wind, nor water to quench thirst, nor a sweet-tempered breeze. There shall be no evening to rest from labor, nor night to cease from work, nor the tranquility of finished deeds to look upon with satisfaction. There shall be no common partaking of food; no winter to prepare the earth, no spring to bring forth the birth of the land's preparation, no heat of summer, nor autumn to care for the ripening of fruit. There shall be no hail in the violence of the air, nor rain to make the grass grow, nor dew for the comfort of plants, nor morning which marks the light of day, nor the storehouse of night to reveal the darkness—but only the crown of glory as the joy of the righteous.

But for the ungodly: unquenchable fire, and **eternal gloom** <note>original: "աշխամուղջ յաւիտենից" — "ashkhamughj" is a specific Classical Armenian term for a thick, heavy darkness or fog, often used to describe the atmosphere of the underworld.</note>, and perpetual torments; this is the judgment.

I gave an answer, sighing deeply, and I said: "Blessed are those who endured for this short time for the sake of the height of glory. But woe to us! For we, during this short time, performed the will of our flesh, and now we enter into eternal torments and are tortured in unquenchable fire forever. It would have been better if we had not been born at all! Who among living humans has not sinned? Or who among those born has not transgressed His command? As I see it, that world of joy is for only a few, but for many there are torments, for all of us together are drenched in lawlessness."

<meta>catchword: gna- (will go-)</meta>

<summary>Ezra describes the Day of Judgment as a timeless state where the natural elements of the world cease to exist, leaving only the reward of the righteous and the punishment of the wicked. Overwhelmed by the strictness of this justice, Ezra laments that most of humanity is destined for suffering due to their sinful nature.</summary>

# E Z R A #

...our souls. Shall we go to a place of torments, or shall we be in a state of rest until the day of judgment? Or shall we enter into torments from this moment forth?
He answered and said: I will tell you this as well. Do not count yourself among the condemned <note>original: "մահապարտսն" — those deserving of death or the "guilty," referring to the spiritually lost.</note>, for for you and those like you, a treasury full of good things is prepared, which will not be revealed to you until the end of times.
Hear now concerning what you asked; this is the matter: When the decree of death goes forth from the Most High to take the human soul, immediately the breath is separated from the body and goes to its assigned place. And if it is full of good works and has kept the commandments of the Most High <note>original: "բարձրելոյն" — a standard epithet for God in this literature.</note>, even though it dwelt for a time in a corruptible nature within a mortal body <note>original: "կնական մարմնոյն" — literally "born of woman," an idiom for the physical, mortal human condition.</note>, yet it served with blamelessness in steadfastness through every hour of trial. Such a soul rejoices and is glad in its rest in the **sevenfold path**:

**The first path:** that it struggled with much labor against every sin.
**The second path:** seeing the punishments prepared for the sinners.
**The third path:** the testimony which God testifies to it, that with great faith it kept the laws which were given to it.
**The fourth path:** in which the prepared good things are revealed to it, how it is kept in great peace, served by the angels.
**The fifth path:** it is glorified with joy, because it has stripped off corruption; and from then on it is counted among the angels to inherit the eternal light.
**The sixth path:** in which it is shown how its face shines like the sun, and thereafter shall not be darkened by corruption.
**The seventh path:** which is above all paths, in which it exults with confidence and boldness, not feeling shame or being abashed, but rejoicing it hastens to see the face of God, whom it served in blamelessness during its life, by whom it is to be glorified and receive the reward of compensation. These are the paths of the souls of the righteous.

But as for the souls of the ungodly, and those who did not keep the commandments of the Most High, and despised His laws, and loathed His servants; they shall not enter into the place of rest forever. Instead, immediately once the souls are separated from the body, they shall enter into eternal torments through **seven paths** with sorrow and grief:

**The first path:** because they abandoned the laws and changed the commands of the Most High.
**The second path:** because they did not wish to turn and repent while they were still in this world.
**The third path:** in which they are distressed, seeing the righteous in rest and their own torments.

I said: "I beseech you, permit me to ask this also: On the day of judgment, can the righteous intercede for the ungodly <note>original: "ամբարիշտն" — those without piety or the wicked.</note>, or offer prayers for them? -> ### THE THIRD <-

For if He does not reproach and punish the false multitude <note>original: "զբազմութն ստակականն" — this refers to those who are insincere or hypocritical in their faith</note>, no one from the many would enter beyond the limit. <margin>1</margin> He answered and said to me, "Do not speak of that which is higher than you. <term>Chapter 8</term> Do not be a hypocrite before God. Understand what has been commanded of you. For although foreknowledge from Him is abundant, He granted free will to mankind—the knowledge of the deed—so they would know what they do, so they might not be punished. Why did those who have the same body and the same impulse of passions not imitate the righteous? Not only did they not walk in their way, but they also despised them and loathed their way of life. -> ### EZRA <-

<margin>10</margin> ...in its own time, the child <note>or infant</note> whom He commanded to be born, until the time of the witness <note>original: "վկայութեան" — likely referring to the fulfillment of the term of birth or the manifestation of life</note>; <margin>11</margin> and after that, to guide him with His wisdom, <margin>12</margin> and to feed him with the fruit of His womb <note>original: "բերովք պտղոյ իւրոյ" — referring to natural sustenance or milk</note>, and to discipline him with His examples, and little by little to increase in him wisdom and the knowledge of all evil and good, and those things which are not likewise. <margin>13</margin> And after all this, to let him die. <margin>14</margin> In such a way He has authority over His works. But if He then destroys him after he was created and born through so much time with labor, and nourished with pains and toil, and disciplined with gentle laws, what profit would there be? <margin>15</margin> And while I was thinking upon these things, I opened my mouth and began to entreat the Most High, saying: "Lord God, as the God of your works, have mercy; and upon your creatures. And be a helper to your possessions, and even more so to your people, <margin>16</margin> for whom I mourn; and to your inheritance, for which I am grieved; and for the nation of Eli <note>original: "ազգիս Էլի" — this is an abbreviated form of 'Israel' commonly found in Armenian manuscripts</note>, for which I mourn; and for the seed of Abraham, for which I am troubled. Look upon us, and reconcile us and our transgressions, <margin>18</margin> for I have perceived the great destruction <note>original: "զանինայութիւն" — meaning ruin or lack of mercy/pity</note> which is to come in the future. <margin>19</margin> Therefore, O Creator of all, long-suffering Most High, hear my voice and give ear to my words which I speak before you, while I stand in prayer before you."

<meta>Continuity: This page continues the "Prayer of Ezra" (4 Ezra 8:26-36). Ezra is pleading with God to focus on those who fear Him and keep His covenants, rather than those who have lived wickedly. The text emphasizes God's reputation as "Merciful" and "Compassionate," arguing that God's grace is best demonstrated through the forgiveness of sinners who have no merits of their own.</meta>

-> ### THIRD <-

...their lawless works, but for those who kept your covenants with fear, spare them; and do not consider those who walked in wickedness before you. But remember those who willingly knew your fear; and do not desire to destroy those who made their habits like those of animals, but look with compassion on your servants who have hoped in your glory. For we and those before us have worked the deeds of death by our will, but you, Lord, Lover of Mankind <note>original: "մարդասէր" (mardasēr) — a title for God emphasizing His love and philanthropy toward humanity</note>, were called patient for us sinners. For although we were of such a kind in our good works, and did nothing according to your will, but followed the uncleanness of the flesh, you will have compassion to show mercy; then you shall be called Merciful. For those who worked holiness by your holy will are not in need of mercy, for they have the reward of repayment for their <margin>1</margin> works. 

<margin>2</margin> What are we humans, that you should be angry with us in truth? <margin>3</margin> There is no one born on earth who has not sinned. <margin>4</margin> In this your compassion shall be known, when you show mercy and pardon us, and <margin>5</margin> forgive our impieties, which do not have the substance <note>original: "հիւթ" (hyut‘) — juice, essence, or vital moisture; here meaning the "stuff" or "merit" of good deeds</note> of good works.

<margin>7</margin> The Lord answered me and said to me: If sinners return to me <margin>8</margin> with all their heart, I <margin>3</margin> will not think to repay their former sins. But at the end of the departure of their souls, as I find them, so I shall judge. And thus I will be glad in those who return to good <margin>9</margin> works, as I am glad in my righteous ones. 

<margin>1</margin> Compare me to a simple farmer: just as a farmer plows and plants as much as he wishes and is willing, and takes care of each in its time as is proper. Though some of them may become weak and approach corruption <note>original: "յապականուե" — refers to the decay or perishing of plants</note>, he takes care of them. And if the care prevails, he rejoices with joy, because that which was going to weaken became strong. But if it is of no use in the proper time, the care will be put away full of sadness. Thus shall it be upon the earth: the Most High will be patient over them; for if they repent of the things they did unlawfully and do good, [they shall live]; <margin>12</margin> otherwise they shall be punished. 

I answered and said: Since you have once permitted me to speak before you, <margin>13</margin> I beseech you, tell me, your servant: if the seeds of the farmer do not receive the rain in measure, they dry up. <margin>14</margin> Likewise, the person to whom you do not show mercy cannot survive. <margin>15</margin> Therefore, spare your people, Lord, and have mercy on your inheritance; have mercy on your possessions and the works of your hands. 

<margin>16</margin> He answered and said to me: <margin>20</margin> In misery shall the people be miserable who dwell in this world, because many years... <note>The text cuts off here at the catchword</note>

<meta>Catchword: am- (likely "amaneals" - years spent/passed)</meta>

<summary>In this passage, Ezra argues that God's mercy is truly proven by His forgiveness of sinners rather than the righteous. God responds with a parable of a farmer, explaining that while He is patient and seeks to nurture souls, those who fail to "take root" in goodness will ultimately face judgment.</summary>

### E Z R A ###

...they walked in impiety; and concerning the coming death, no knowledge was found in any of them. * But as for you, think for yourself, <margin>51</margin> and concerning the glory that remains for you, take heart. * For the true <margin>52</margin> paradise lies open for you, and the tree of the true paradise is planted; life is prepared for the coming delight; the city is built, the rest is ordained, goodness is adorned, and sickness is sealed away from you. * Death is abolished from you; hell has <margin>53</margin> been put to shame; corruption is chased away from us. * All labor is <margin>54</margin> separated from you; and the treasures of immortality have been revealed to you. * Do not pray any more for the destruction of the people. <margin>55</margin> * For just as these things are prepared for you—as I said <margin>59</margin> above—likewise for them, preparations are made for their coming torments. * I made man so that he might keep my commands, and <margin>60</margin> that he might reflect upon eternal death, yet at all times they have continually embittered me. * Because of this, my judgment is firm. <margin>61</margin>

And I spoke with the Lord and said: I beseech you, Lord, speak with the wretched people, so that they may hear from you and believe; that they might fear and return, and not perish, but rather live. For if anyone else speaks, perhaps they will not believe this from among men. The Lord answered and said: At all times I have revealed myself to my servants who are pleasing to me, and I spoke with those worthy of me. But to others, I made myself known through the hands of men. I am the Lord who searches the hearts and the kidneys <note>original: "երիկամունս" (erikamuns) — in biblical thought, the kidneys (or "reins") were considered the seat of a person's most secret emotions and intentions</note>, and I know man even before they exist in the womb. I know that if I speak to them face to face, they will not obey, but will become even more stubborn in their rebellion. 

I answered the Lord and said: I ask of you, Most High, why was such a heart not given to us, so that we might know only the good, and do only that, and desire only that, and know only it as sweet? But when we received the knowledge of evil, we then desired that which you hate. Why then did you create man at all, if we were to have that [knowledge] and sin by it? The Lord answered me and said: I made man so that he should not perish, but that he might live this life with honor and inherit that [future] life. And like my angels, I gave him wisdom to know what is good and what is evil. I honored him and gave him authority to do whatever he willed. And I made subject to him all that is under the heavens, that he might rule over them. I gave laws and commandments so that they might be able to live here, or there obtain the immortal goods. But he took such authority from me; that which was created well, [he used] not well...

<summary>God responds to Ezra's plea, explaining that while Paradise is prepared for the righteous, the wicked have chosen to ignore God's commands despite their given wisdom. Ezra questions why God gave humans the capacity to know evil, to which God responds by emphasizing the gift of free will and the honor of human dominion.</summary>

->### T H I R D ###<-

...he used them for evil and sinned. It is not that anything was created as an evil thing, but everything that I made was very good; each thing that came to be was made for its own proper use. For just as iron was made, not so that it might kill, but so that it might work the earth and be for the benefit of mankind; yet humans did not remain in that for which they were created, but they set their hands to that which was not a good work. Likewise, they transformed other good things into evil. Therefore, the one who created good things is not the cause <note>The "cause" here refers to the source of evil; God argues that the Creator is blameless for the misuse of His creations.</note>, but the one who did not enjoy them properly has insulted their Creator. For this reason, their torments remain for them; for all those who have been made by me ought to have known me, being guided by these very things. Indeed, even those who did not enjoy these things well should have recognized me. Stop now, <margin>63</margin> and do not be concerned for them anymore. * I answered and said: I beseech you, Lord, you who do not hold a grudge, my soul cannot endure not questioning you. For this reason, hear your servant. You have shown me a great multitude of signs, but you have not told me when it shall be, or at what hour.

<margin>1</margin> The Lord answered and said to me: By measuring, mark the specific arrival of the signs; and it shall be, when you see that a portion <margin>2</margin> of them has passed, * then you will understand that the end is near. It is necessary that those signs which were spoken of happen first, and <margin>3</margin> in that way, the end shall come. * When the time draws near, there shall be commotion among peoples, the movement of places among the nations, the deceit of leaders, the wavering of the holy ones <note>original: "սբց" (սրբոց) — referring to the trembling or instability of the righteous or the saints during times of trial</note>, the persecution of priests, the perversion of the Holy Faith, and the doubt of the people. There shall be confusion among the nations, distress in the cities, the sparking of fires in various places, and great trembling. There shall be the separation of various nations, cities, and villages, and an increase of errors caused by <margin>8</margin> foul spirits. * Then you will understand that the end is near. * And whoever is found worthy by me at that time shall survive and see my salvation, and the new earth, and my borders <margin>9</margin> which I sanctified before the ages. * And then those who have been scornful shall see and shall lament and be amazed—those who now see my ways <note>referring to the path of righteousness or the divine laws</note>. For this reason, the prepared judgment stays and remains for them, because they did not recognize the grace of my laws, nor did they keep everything <margin>13</margin> that was written in them. * But as for you, do not mix yourself <margin>14</margin> with such as these, whom the flame of fire is to burn. * I answered <margin>15</margin> and said: * As I have said many times, there are many who are lost, and few who are saved—and those only with great labor. Who can prepare themselves with such caution as your laws command? The Lord answered and said: I have commanded nothing beyond the reach of man, and not...

<summary>God explains that evil arises from the misuse of a good creation and describes the apocalyptic signs—including social chaos and natural disasters—that will precede the final judgment. Ezra laments the difficulty of salvation, noting that while many are lost, only a few are saved through great effort.</summary>

->### E Z R A ###<-

...is not impossible. But I tell you briefly: just as you wish to be honored by your servant, so you also should behave toward the living God. And what seems evil to you, do not do to your neighbor <note>This is a version of the "Golden Rule," phrased negatively: "Do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself."</note>. And just as you wish to be treated with kindness, if you love the same, you should do so as well. For if it seems wrong to you to suffer such a thing from your brother, then do not do it to him either. For I have commanded your own ways to you: for as the will is, so are the works; and as the works are, so is the reward. Let the senseless and mindless nation perish, but let the precious ones and the pearls <note>The "pearls" refers to the small remnant of righteous souls who are valued by God.</note> be saved. For I do not desire the multitude of the impious as much as I long for the few and the holy. Thus shall it be, and thus it shall stand; it has been so decreed by me, and nothing of these things shall pass away until the judgment occurs and the conclusion of my words.

And when the Lord ceased speaking with me, I saw the glory of the Most High, ten thousand times brighter than the sun. At that time, fear and trembling still held me. In the midst of that glory, the angel who had spoken with me at the first came to me, strengthened me, and restored my senses to me. And he gave me a command and said: "Do not fear and do not tremble, for you have found great grace before God. * Stay here for seven more days, * <margin>23</margin> and go out into the field where there is no house or roof, nor anything else, <margin>24</margin> but only flowers. And do not taste anything except for the flowers of the field where you will be. * And pray <margin>25</margin> to the Most High without ceasing, and after that, I will come to you." * <margin>26</margin>

And I went, according to his word, into the field to the place called Ardab <note>In other versions of the book of Ezra, this field is called Ardat or Arphad. And I sat there among the flowers, and I ate of them; and the taste of them was sweet to me, and they satisfied me and became the strength of my power. * <margin>27</margin> And it happened after several days, while I was reclining upon the grass, my heart was again troubled within me as before. * <margin>28</margin> And my mouth was opened, and I began to speak before the Most High and said: * <margin>29</margin> "O Lord God, who are the creator of all spirits, you clearly revealed yourself to our fathers in the wilderness when they came out of Egypt, passing through the waterless and fruitless desert. <margin>41</margin> She answered and said to me, * "Allow me, my lord, to weep for myself and to continue my mourning; for I am very bitter <margin>42</margin> in my soul and I am full of misery." * And I said to her, <margin>43</margin> "Tell me, what happened?" <margin>1</margin> And it came to pass, as the son entered his wedding chamber, he fell and <margin>2</margin> died. * And we extinguished the lights, and in place of great joy, immeasurable mourning arose. -> ### THIRD VISION <-

[He sp]oke like a man, and I shall speak with you. And I said:

We glorify the entrance of your door; we glorify your resurrection, which was shown to us; we glorify your ways. We glorify your seed, the word, the grace, the faith, the salt <note>original: "զաղն" (z-ałn). Reference to the "salt of the earth" (Matthew 5:13)</note>, the ungraspable pearl <note>original: "զանհաս մարգարիտն" (zanhas margaritn). A reference to the "pearl of great price" (Matthew 13:46)</note>, the treasure, the plow, the net, the greatness—you who for our sake were called the Son of Man—the truth, the rest, the knowledge, the power, the commandment, the boldness, the freedom, and the flight unto you. For you are the Lord, the root of immortality and the fountain of incorruptibility, and the foundation of the ages; you were named all of these things for our sake. So that we, calling upon you by these names, might know your greatness, which is invisible to us in this present time, but is visible only to the saints, as it was portrayed in your unique humanity.

**9.** And having broken the bread, he offered it to them; and by making a prayer over each of the brothers, they became worthy of the Lord's grace and of the holy thanksgiving. He also partook in the same manner and said: "May I also have a portion with you, and peace be with you, my beloved." And he said to Byrrhus <note>Byrrhus is a traditional disciple/scribe of the Apostle John in apocryphal literature</note>: "Take two of the brothers with you, along with two youths, and shovels, and follow me." And Byrrhus, without delay, did exactly as John, the servant of God, had commanded him. And the blessed John, leaving the house, walked before the doors; he commanded the multitude to move away from him. And reaching the tomb of a certain brother of ours, he said to the youths: "Dig, my children." And they began to dig. But he urged them on, saying: "Let the digging be deeper." and while they were digging, he spoke to them the word of life and exhorted those of the church who were with him in the house, building them up and establishing them in the greatness of the Lord, and making prayers over each one of them. But we understood nothing at all.

# OF JOHN
Vv 2

...O You who gave rest and drove away the disturber within me. O You who established my blameless rest in You. O You who kept my paths in You without stumbling. O You who gave me an unwavering faith in You. O You who defined Your knowledge within me. O You who repay the reward for each one’s works. O You who placed it in my soul to consider no possession more precious than You.

**9.** And now, Lord Jesus Christ, I have completed the stewardship <note>original: "մատակարարութիւն" (matakararutyun). Refers to his apostolic mission or ministry</note> which I received from You; make me worthy of Your rest, granting me Your mercy, which is inescapable and ineffable salvation. And in my coming to You, let the fire shrink back; let the darkness be driven away; let the abyss grow weak; let the furnace be silenced; let Gehenna be extinguished; let the angels of the evil one be ashamed; let the demons fear; let the princes be terrified; let their powers be subdued; let those on the right hand stand; let those on the left hand not remain. Let the slanderer be silenced; let Satan be horrified; let his wrath be scorched; let his error be submerged; let his torments be abashed; let his attacks be bound; let his children be tortured; and let his every root be confounded and mourn forever.

**10.** And grant me to complete my path to You blameless and uncoerced; to receive that which You promised to those who live in holiness and love You with modesty. And then, having sealed his whole self <note>This refers to the "Seal" or the Sign of the Cross made over his entire body</note>, he said: "May You be with me, my Lord Jesus Christ." And he lay down in the deep pit, where he had spread his garments. And having said to us: "Peace be with you, brothers." And while we were both rejoicing and weeping, the holy Apostle and Evangelist John surrendered his spirit into the hand of the Lord. And to Jesus be glory, and to Christ honor, and power forever and ever. Amen.

# THE PETITION OF ETHAGH <note>original: "Եթաղի" (Et'aghi). This name may refer to a specific editor or a variant of a name associated with the transmission of the text.</note>

Everywhere and in all things there is a season; a year comes and reaches this world, and returns again to its rest. But only the one who conquers trials conquers the time. Do not be arrogant when you are in desirable glory, and do not be stingy <note>original: "գձուձ" (gdzudz) - meaning small-minded or miserly</note> when you reach misfortune. For if you hold the balance thus, you will be a just balancer of the life of this world. For we fall into harms not through simple things, nor through our members <note>Refers to the physical body or joints</note>, but through many and impossible and various bitternesses; and there is no one who can be a comforter to us. We have missed all suspicious goods at once—from the world, and from life, and from greatness; and I have found only ignorance as an assistant to evils.

And now, O soul, you were surrounded by many, many sorrows; do not lose heart in the labor. But endure, O beloved, considering it as a thing brought to mind: that one does not do what one wills and thinks, but rather suffers that which one does not seek and flees from. But the divine decree <term>Atheghēn sahman</term> <note>Literally "divine boundary," referring to God's providence or fate</note> intends to conquer all. Someone said, and told us this—Plato <note>original: "պլետիկոս" (Pletikos) - a common medieval Armenian corruption of the name Plato</note> in one chapter: "If there is hope for the living, the hopeless die." If it be so, it is necessary to endure sorrows and bear trials with virtue. For there is nothing, and there is nothing in the life of those born on earth, and nothing in the stability of human affairs remains; but like a wheel, everything turns and moves.

And now, I, grieving in mind about all this, write to my own self and to my foster-father <note>original: "սնունդ հօր" (snund hor) - can refer to a spiritual mentor or a guardian</note> concerning my many miseries. Woe is me when I consider the changes! I see all things of men as human things; and only one faithful hope is left to me, and that is love for humanity <term>Mardasirut’iwn</term> <note>A significant theological term describing God’s innate love for mankind</note> alone.

---

* *Some say: "Only in the year does he conquer." Some say: "Just balancer of the life of Jesus." Some say: "From all opinions of these goods... from the world and from glory and from greatness... you were defeated by many sorrows, O soul." Some say: "My misfortunes... I see as a man."*

->THE END OF THE ADDITIONS<-

# Decorative Illustration: Marbled Paper

<note>This image is a black-and-white reproduction of what was originally a vibrant, multicolored sheet of marbled paper.</note>

This page consists of a full-page decorative pattern, a style known as **marbled paper**. This specific design is a **"nonpareil"** or **"comb"** pattern. It is created by floating pigments on a liquid surface and using a comb-like tool to draw the colors into rhythmic, repeating shapes before transferring them onto the paper.

The pattern is characterized by:
*   Dense, repeating vertical columns.
*   Small, overlapping semi-circular arches or "fans."
*   Fine, concentric lines that create an undulating, wavy texture across the entire surface.

Such decorative papers were a hallmark of high-quality <term>bookbinding</term> (the art of physically assembling a book). They were most commonly used as <term>endpapers</term>—the pages at the very beginning or end of a volume that connect the inner pages to the heavy outer covers—or as decorative covers themselves. This pattern provides a visual rest for the reader and demonstrates the craftsmanship involved in the book's production.

<summary>This page features a decorative nonpareil marbled paper pattern, traditionally used in bookbinding as an endpaper or cover decoration.</summary>
<keywords>marbled paper, nonpareil pattern, comb marbling, bookbinding, endpaper, decorative arts</keywords>

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the <term>copyright</term> (legal ownership of intellectual property) to expire and the book to enter the <term>public domain</term>. A <term>public domain</term> book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has ended. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary from country to country. These books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture, and knowledge that is often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations, and other <term>marginalia</term> (notes written in the margins) present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## **Usage guidelines**

Google is proud to partner with libraries to <term>digitize</term> (convert to digital format) public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

*   *Make non-commercial use of the files* — We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
*   *Refrain from automated querying* — Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system. If you are conducting research on <term>machine translation</term> (using software to translate languages), <term>optical character recognition</term> (OCR, or converting images of text into searchable data), or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
*   *Maintain attribution* — The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
*   *Keep it legal* — Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we cannot offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

These marks are a reminder of the book’s long life—from its first printing to the library where it lived, and finally to this digital version.

We ask that you:

+ *Use these files for personal use only* 
We created Google Book Search for individuals. Please use these files for your own personal, non-commercial research or enjoyment.

+ *Do not use automated search tools* 
Do not send automated programs to search Google’s systems. # Google

This is a digital copy of a book that was kept for many generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google. This work is part of a large-scale project intended to make the world’s books easy to find and read online.

This volume has survived long enough for its <term>copyright</term> <note>A legal protection that gives the creator of a work exclusive rights to its use and distribution.</note> to expire, allowing it to enter the <term>public domain</term> <note>The state of belonging to the public as a whole, rather than an individual or company; these works are free for anyone to use.</note>. A public domain book is one that was never protected by copyright or whose legal protection time has run out. Whether a book is in the public domain can change depending on which country you are in. These books are our windows into the past, holding a treasure trove of history, culture, and knowledge that is often hard to find elsewhere.

Handwritten marks, stamps, and other <term>marginalia</term> <note>Notes or symbols written in the margins of a book by previous owners or librarians.</note> found in the original physical volume are included in this file. These are reminders of the book’s long life—traveling from the original publisher to a library, and finally to your screen.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to <term>digitize</term> <note>The process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be viewed on a computer.</note> public domain materials and make them available to everyone. Public domain books belong to the community, and we act simply as their <term>custodians</term> <note>Guardians or caretakers who look after something on behalf of others.</note>. However, this process is expensive. To keep providing this service, we have set certain rules to prevent commercial abuse, such as technical limits on <term>automated querying</term> <note>The use of computer programs to automatically search or download large amounts of data without human intervention.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We created Google Book Search for individual readers. We ask that you use these files only for your own personal, non-business purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Please do not send automated searches of any kind to Google’s servers. If you are a researcher working on projects like machine translation or <term>optical character recognition</term> <note>A technology that allows computers to "read" and convert images of text into searchable data.</note>, please contact us. We support the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to assist you.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" <note>A faint identifying image or text embedded in a digital file to show its source.</note> that you see on each page is necessary to let people know about this project and help them find more books. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever you do with these files, remember that you are responsible for making sure your actions are legal. Just because we believe a book is in the public domain in the United States does not mean it is free to use in other countries. Copyright laws vary globally, and we cannot give advice on whether a specific use is permitted. Please do not assume that a book’s presence in Google Book Search means it can be used however you like anywhere in the world. The legal consequences for <term>copyright infringement</term> <note>The unauthorized use of protected material, which can lead to significant legal penalties.</note> can be very serious.

This includes technical limits on <term>automated querying</term> <note>The use of computer programs to quickly scan or download large amounts of data without human intervention.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* 
We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals. We ask that you use these files only for your own personal, non-business purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* 
Please do not send automated searches of any kind to Google’s system. If you are conducting research involving <term>machine translation</term> <note>Using software to translate text from one language to another.</note> or <term>optical character recognition</term> <note>Also known as OCR; the technology that turns images of typed or handwritten text into data that a computer can "read" and search.</note>, please contact us. We support the use of public domain materials for these purposes.

+ *Maintain attribution* 
The Google "watermark" <note>A faint identifying image or text placed on a digital file to show its source.</note> you see on each file is necessary to tell people about this project and help them find more books. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* 
You are responsible for making sure your use of this book is legal in your country. Do not assume that because a book is in the public domain in the United States, it is free to use everywhere else. Laws vary by region, and we cannot give legal advice on whether a specific use is allowed. Copyright laws are strict, and the penalties for breaking them can be severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to <term>digitize</term> <note>The process of converting a physical document into a digital image or text format.</note> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their <term>custodians</term> <note>Guardians or caretakers of something valuable.</note>. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on <term>automated querying</term> <note>The use of software or "bots" to automatically search or download data at high speeds.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, <term>optical character recognition</term> <note>Often abbreviated as OCR, this is the technology used to convert images of text into editable, searchable text data.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. <term>Copyright infringement</term> <note>The illegal use of copyrighted material, which can result in significant legal penalties.</note> liability can be quite severe.

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be processed by a computer.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>Often abbreviated as OCR, this is the technology used to convert images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” <term>watermark: a faint design or text identifying the source of a document, often used to prevent unauthorized use or to provide credit.</term> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.
