This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the <term>copyright: a legal framework that grants creators exclusive rights to their work for a specific duration</term> to expire and the book to enter the <term>public domain: the state of creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws and are available for use by the general public</term>. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture, and knowledge that is often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations, and other <term>marginalia: handwritten notes or scribbles made by previous readers or owners in the margins of a book</term> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to digitize public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying <note>Automated querying refers to the use of computer scripts or "bots" to download or crawl through pages at a high speed, which can strain digital infrastructure.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is the technology used to convert images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we cannot offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to <term>digitize: the process of converting physical materials, such as paper documents or books, into digital images or text</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on <term>automated querying: the use of software scripts or "bots" to automatically search or download content</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on <term>machine translation: the use of software to translate text or speech from one language to another</term>, <term>optical character recognition: (OCR) the electronic conversion of images of typed, handwritten or printed text into machine-encoded text</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. <term>Copyright infringement: the use of works protected by copyright law without permission, infringing certain exclusive rights granted to the copyright holder</term> liability can be quite severe.

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>often abbreviated as OCR; the technology that allows a computer to "read" text from an image or scan</note>, or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <note>The use of computer scripts or "bots" to search or download data automatically without human intervention.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, **optical character recognition** <note>Often abbreviated as OCR; technology that converts different types of documents, such as scanned paper documents or PDF files, into editable and searchable data.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "**watermark**" <note>A faint identifying image or text embedded in the digital file to show its origin.</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitization</term> <note>The process of converting physical text and images into a digital format that can be processed by a computer.</note> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated Querying</term> <note>The use of software programs to search or download data from a system automatically, which can overwhelm the service.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, **optical character recognition** <term>OCR</term> <note>The electronic or mechanical conversion of images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Infringement</term> <note>The act of breaking the terms of a law or agreement; in this case, violating the legal rights of a copyright holder.</note> liability can be quite severe.

This is a **digital copy** <term>an electronic version</term> of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world's books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>legal ownership of creative content</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>works available for anyone to use</term> <note>A book enters the public domain when its legal protections expire, allowing the public to freely access and share it as part of our collective cultural history.</note>. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that's often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other marginalia present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book's long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>convert to digital format</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>software-driven searching</term> <note>This refers to the use of "bots" or automated scripts to download data, which can strain the system.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <note>The use of computer software to translate text between different languages.</note>, **optical character recognition** <term>OCR</term> <note>Technology that identifies printed letters in an image and turns them into editable text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google **“watermark”** <gloss>digital identifying mark</gloss> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>the use of software scripts or "bots" to search a database at high speeds</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>using computers to translate text between languages</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>OCR; technology that turns images of text into searchable data</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>the unauthorized use of works under copyright</term> liability can be quite severe.

Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated Querying: Using computer scripts or programs to automatically search and download files at high speeds.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <note>Using computers to automatically translate text from one language to another.</note>, **optical character recognition** <note>OCR: Technology that allows a computer to "read" the text in an image.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" <note>A faint logo or text identifying the source of the document.</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement liability** <note>The legal penalties and fines one might face for using protected material without permission.</note> can be quite severe.

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>Copyright: A legal status that gives creators exclusive rights to their work for a set period of time.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>Public Domain: Creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws, allowing the public to use them freely.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <note>original: "marginalia"; these are handwritten notes, stamps, or comments made by previous readers or librarians in the margins of the physical book.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file - a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## **Usage guidelines**

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitization: The process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be stored and viewed on a computer.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, **optical character recognition** <term>OCR: A technology that recognizes text within a digital image, such as a scanned page, and turns it into editable text.</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully **scanned** <term>Scanning: The process of using light sensors to capture an image of a physical page and convert it into a digital file.</term> by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>Copyright: A legal right that grants the creator of an original work exclusive rights to its use and distribution for a specific period.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>Public Domain: Works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws, allowing the public to use them freely.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. ## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitization: The process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be stored and processed by a computer.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated Querying: Using a computer program to send many rapid requests for information to a system, which can overwhelm the service.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>Also known as OCR; the technology that lets computers "read" printed or handwritten text from images.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

+ **Maintain attribution** The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ **Keep it legal** Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Copyright infringement: The use of works protected by copyright law without permission, infringing on certain exclusive rights, such as the right to reproduce or distribute the protected work.</term> liability can be quite severe.

This is a **digital copy** <term>Digital copy: An electronic version of a physical book, created by scanning the original pages so they can be viewed on computers and other devices.</term> of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>Copyright: A legal protection that gives the creator of a work exclusive rights to its use and distribution for a specific length of time.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>Public domain: Creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws, allowing the public to freely use, share, and adapt them.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginal notes** <note>original: "marginalia" (Latin). This refers to the handwritten notes, sketches, or comments made by readers in the margins of a book's pages over the centuries.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitize: The process of converting physical materials into a digital form so they can be preserved and shared electronically.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their **custodians** <term>Custodians: People or organizations that have responsibility for taking care of something, like a museum guarding its collection.</term>. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated querying: Using a computer program to automatically send many search requests at once, which can slow down the system for everyone else.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, **non-commercial** <term>Non-commercial: Use that is not intended to make money or serve a business interest.</term> purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <note>The use of software to translate text or speech from one language to another.</note>, **optical character recognition** <note>Often abbreviated as OCR; the electronic conversion of images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Copyright infringement: Using someone's protected creative work without their permission in a way that breaks the law.</term> liability <note>Legal responsibility for an action or debt.</note> can be quite severe.

Google’s mission is to organize the world’s information and to make it universally accessible and useful. Google Book Search helps readers discover the world’s books while helping authors and publishers reach new audiences. # Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitize: The process of converting physical materials, like paper books, into a digital format that can be stored and read on a computer.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated querying: Using computer programs or "bots" to automatically search or download large amounts of data, which can strain systems.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system. If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>OCR: Technology that converts images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Copyright infringement: Using someone else's copyrighted work without permission in a way that violates their exclusive legal rights.</term> liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitize: The process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be processed by a computer.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>Machine translation: The use of software and artificial intelligence to translate text from one language to another without human intervention.</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>Optical character recognition (OCR): Technology used to convert different types of documents, such as scanned paper documents or PDF files, into editable and searchable data.</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitize: The process of converting physical materials into a digital format, such as an image or electronic text.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their **custodians** <term>Custodians: People or organizations responsible for the care and protection of something, in this case, historical texts.</term>. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated querying: Using computer programs or scripts to automatically send requests or search for information, which can overwhelm a system's resources.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, **non-commercial** <term>Non-commercial: Activity that is not intended for or directed toward commercial advantage or monetary compensation.</term> purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>Machine translation: The use of software to translate text or speech from one language to another.</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>Optical Character Recognition (OCR): The electronic conversion of images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-encoded text.</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Whether a book is still in **copyright** <term>Copyright: Legal protection for original works, giving the creator exclusive rights to their use.</term> varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement liability** <term>Copyright infringement liability: The legal responsibility or penalty one faces for violating the exclusive rights of a copyright holder.</term> can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitization: The process of converting physical text or images into a digital format.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated querying: Using computer programs or scripts to automatically send search requests to a system, rather than a person doing it manually.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Copyright infringement: Using or distributing copyrighted material without the legal permission of the owner, which can lead to legal penalties.</term> liability can be quite severe.

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitization: The process of converting physical text or images into a digital format.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying <term>Automated querying: Using software programs or "bots" to send many requests to a website very quickly.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>Machine translation: The use of software to translate text from one language to another.</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>Optical character recognition (OCR): The technology used to convert images of printed or handwritten text into machine-readable text.</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "**watermark**" <note>A watermark is a faint, identifying image or pattern in a digital file that appears behind the main text to identify the creator or source.</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Copyright infringement: Using someone else's copyrighted work without permission, which can lead to legal penalties.</term> liability can be quite severe.

Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>OCR: Technology used to convert different types of documents, such as scanned paper documents or PDF files, into editable and searchable data.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on <term>automated querying</term> <note>The use of computer scripts or software to automatically search or download data without human intervention.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on <term>machine translation</term> <note>The use of software to translate text from one language to another.</note>, <term>optical character recognition</term> <note>The process of converting images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. <term>Copyright infringement</term> <note>The use of works protected by copyright law without permission, which can lead to legal penalties.</note> liability can be quite severe.

<image-desc>The multi-colored Google logo.</image-desc>

This is a <term>digital copy</term> <note>A digital surrogate created by scanning a physical object, allowing historical texts to be read on modern screens.</note> of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the <term>copyright</term> <note>A legal status that grants the creator of a work exclusive rights to its use; when this expires, the work enters the public domain.</note> to expire and the book to enter the <term>public domain</term> <note>Works whose intellectual property rights have expired or been forfeited, meaning they belong to the public and can be freely used by anyone.</note>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other <term>marginalia</term> <note>Handwritten notes, sketches, or comments made by previous owners or readers in the margins of a book, which provide a history of the book's ownership and use.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file - a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to <term>digitize</term> <note>The process of converting physical text and images into a digital format that can be processed by a computer.</note> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on <term>machine translation</term> <note>The use of software to translate text from one language to another.</note>, <term>optical character recognition</term> <note>Often abbreviated as OCR, this technology converts images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## About Google Book Search

Google’s mission is to organize the world’s information and to make it universally accessible and useful. Google Book Search helps readers discover the world’s books while helping authors and publishers reach new audiences. This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <note>The legal protection that gives creators and publishers control over how their work is used. Once this term ends, the work enters the public domain.</note> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <note>The status of creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws, meaning they are free for the public to access, use, and build upon.</note>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <note>Handwritten notes, symbols, or comments made by previous readers or librarians in the margins of a book's pages.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file - a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <note>The process of converting physical materials, such as paper books, into a digital format that can be viewed on computers or mobile devices.</note> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <note>The use of software or "bots" to automatically search or scrape data from a system, which can strain resources and violate terms of service.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>Copyright: A legal protection that grants the creator of a work exclusive rights to its use and distribution for a specific period.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>Public Domain: The status of a work that is no longer protected by copyright, making it freely available for any member of the public to use, share, or build upon.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <note>original: "marginalia"; These are the handwritten notes, library stamps, or sketches left in the margins of the physical book by previous readers and custodians over the years.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to digitize public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying <note>Automated querying refers to the use of computer programs or "bots" to rapidly scan or download data, which can interfere with the service's performance.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>OCR (Optical Character Recognition): The technology used to convert images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

This is a **digital copy** <term>Digital copy: An electronic version of a physical book, created through scanning to preserve the text and images for digital access.</term> of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>Copyright: A legal protection that gives creators control over their work; once it expires, the work becomes free for everyone to use.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>Public domain: Creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws and are owned by the public.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <note>original: "marginalia"; This Latin term refers to the handwritten notes, stamps, or drawings left in the margins of a book by previous owners or librarians, often providing clues about its history.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to digitize **public domain** materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their **custodians** <term>Custodians: Guardians or caretakers who look after something valuable, like historical documents, without necessarily owning them.</term>. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated querying: Using computer scripts or "bots" to automatically search or download information at high speeds, which can strain digital systems.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>Often abbreviated as OCR, this technology converts images of text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <note>This refers to the legal liability that arises from using a copyrighted work without the permission of the rights holder.</note> liability can be quite severe.

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>Copyright: A legal right that grants creators and publishers control over how their work is used for a specific period of time.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>Public domain: Creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws; they belong to the community and can be used by anyone without permission.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **notes in the margins** <note>original: "marginalia"; This refers to handwritten notes, stamps, or markings left by previous readers or librarians in the physical book over many years.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to digitize public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated querying: Using software or "bots" to send a high volume of search requests to a computer system, which can overwhelm the service.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <note>The process of using computer software to translate text from one language to another.</note>, **optical character recognition** <note>Often abbreviated as OCR, this technology converts images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" <note>A faint, identifying image or pattern embedded into the digital page to show its origin.</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Copyright infringement: The use of works protected by copyright law without permission, which can result in severe legal liability.</term> liability can be quite severe.

This is a **digital copy** <term>Digital copy: An electronic version of a physical book, created by scanning the original pages so they can be viewed on computers and digital devices.</term> of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>Copyright: A legal right that grants the creator of a work exclusive control over its use; once this period ends, the work enters the public domain.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>Public domain: Works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws, meaning they are free for the public to use, share, and enjoy without permission.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <note>These are handwritten notes, library stamps, or sketches made by previous readers and custodians over the years, which remain visible in the digital scan.</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file - a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

### Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitize: The process of converting physical materials, like paper books, into digital formats such as images or searchable text.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* <note>This refers to using software or "bots" to automatically download or harvest data from the system at high speeds.</note> Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” <note>A faint identifying mark or logo embedded in the digital image to indicate its source.</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage Guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>Digitize: The process of converting physical materials, like paper books or handwritten manuscripts, into electronic formats that can be stored and viewed on computers.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>Automated querying: Using computer software or "bots" to automatically search, scan, or download large amounts of data without a human being present.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes. <note>Essentially, these files are for private study and research, not for resale or business exploitation.</note>

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, **optical character recognition** <term>Optical Character Recognition (OCR): A technology that identifies letters and words in a picture of a page, turning the image into text that a computer can "read" and search.</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it. <note>The watermark serves as a digital breadcrumb, leading other researchers back to the source and acknowledging the effort of the libraries involved.</note>

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in **copyright** <term>Copyright: The legal protection of a creator's work; these laws change depending on which country you are in.</term> varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>Copyright infringement: The illegal use or distribution of material that is still protected by law, which can result in serious legal consequences.</term> liability can be quite severe.

->**Google**™<-
<note>original: "Google TM"; the trademarked logo of the technology company responsible for the digitization.</note>

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>copyright: the legal right that gives the creator of a work exclusive power over its use and distribution for a set period.</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: the state of creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws and are free for public use.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <term>marginalia: notes, marks, or comments written in the margins of a book by previous readers or owners.</term> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitization: the process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be processed by a computer.</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: the use of computer programs to send a large number of search requests to a system or database.</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system. If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>machine translation: the use of software to translate text or speech from one language to another.</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition (OCR): the electronic conversion of images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-encoded text.</term>, or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we cannot offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>copyright infringement: the use of works protected by copyright law without permission, violating the exclusive rights of the copyright holder.</term> liability can be quite severe.

->**Google**™<-
<note>original: "Google TM"; This is the trademarked name of the technology company that performed the digital scanning of this volume.</note>

This is a digital copy of a book that was kept for many generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google. This was done as part of a project to make the world’s books easier to find and explore online.

This book has survived long enough for its **copyright** <term>copyright: a legal right that gives the creator of a work exclusive power over how it is used and shared for a specific period of time.</term> to expire, allowing it to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: the status of creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws and are free for anyone to use without permission.</term>. A public domain book is one that was never protected by copyright or one where the legal protection time has run out. Whether a book is in the public domain can change depending on the country. Public domain books are our windows into the past, holding a vast amount of history, culture, and knowledge that is often difficult to find.

Any marks, notes, or other **marginalia** <term>marginalia: handwritten notes, marks, or comments made in the margins of a book by previous readers or owners.</term> found in the original book will be visible in this file. These are reminders of the book’s long journey from the person who first printed it, to a library, and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to work with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitization: the process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be viewed on a computer.</term> materials that belong to the public and make them widely available. Public domain books belong to the public, and we are simply their caretakers. However, this work is very expensive. To keep providing this service, we have taken steps to prevent commercial companies from using these books unfairly, such as putting technical limits on automated searching.

We also ask that you:

+ *Use these files only for non-commercial purposes* We designed Google Book Search for individuals to use. We ask that you use these files for your own personal, non-business reasons.

+ *Do not use automated searches* Do not send any kind of automated search requests to Google’s system. If you are doing research on things like computer translation or "optical character recognition" (the technology used to read printed text), please contact us. We support using public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Keep the attribution* The Google "watermark" (the small logo or text) you see on each file is very important. It lets people know about the project and helps them find more materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Follow the law* No matter how you use the book, you are responsible for making sure what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that because we believe a book is in the public domain in the United States, it is also in the public domain in other countries. Laws change from place to place, and we cannot tell you if a specific use of a book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s presence on Google Book Search means it can be used however you want anywhere in the world. Breaking copyright laws can lead to serious legal trouble.
