This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the copyright to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: works whose intellectual property rights have expired, allowing them to be freely used, shared, and adapted by the public</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <term>marginalia: handwritten notes, sketches, or comments made by previous owners or readers in the margins of a book's pages</term> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the technical process of converting physical text or images into a digital format for computer storage and viewing</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: the use of computer software or "bots" to search or download data at a high speed without human intervention</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>machine translation: the use of artificial intelligence to translate text from one language to another</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition (OCR): technology that converts images of printed or handwritten text into machine-readable data</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical information, like a printed book, into a digital format that a computer can process</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using computer programs or "bots" to automatically search or download large amounts of data without human intervention</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” <note>This refers to the digital logo or text often placed on the corner of scanned pages to identify the source.</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>copyright infringement: the unauthorized use of works under copyright, which can lead to legal penalties</term> liability can be quite severe.

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be processed and stored by a computer</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using computer programs or "bots" to automatically send many requests to a system, which can strain resources</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition (OCR): the electronic conversion of images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-encoded text</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>copyright infringement: the use of works protected by copyright law without permission, which can result in legal penalties</term> liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical information, like a printed page, into a digital format that a computer can process</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using software scripts or "bots" to search a database or website at high speeds, which can strain computer systems</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>OCR: technology that allows a computer to "read" the text from a scanned image</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.
+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" <note>watermark: a faint identifying image or text embedded in a file to show its origin</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>copyright infringement: the use of works protected by copyright law without permission, which can lead to legal penalties</term> liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to work with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of turning physical items, like paper books, into digital images or text that can be viewed on a computer</term> public domain materials and make them available to everyone. To keep providing this service, we have taken steps to prevent commercial companies from using these files unfairly, including adding technical blocks to prevent automated systems from taking the data.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We created Google Book Search for individuals to use. We ask that you use these files only for your own personal, non-business purposes.
+ *Do not use automated searches* Please do not send automated search requests of any kind to Google's system. We support the use of public domain materials for these types of research and may be able to help you.
+ *Keep the attribution* The Google "watermark" <note>A faint logo or text identifying the source of the file.</note> you see on every page is necessary to let people know about this project and help them find more books. Please do not remove it.

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>copyright: a legal framework that grants creators exclusive rights to their work for a fixed period of time</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: the status of creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws and are free for the public to use</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture, and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations, and other **marginalia** <note>original: "marginalia"; these are handwritten notes, sketches, or comments made by readers in the margins of a book throughout its history</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical text or images into a digital format</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <note>This refers to the use of computer scripts or software to automatically download or search text without human intervention.</note>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>machine translation: the use of software to translate text from one language to another</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition (OCR): the mechanical or electronic conversion of images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-encoded text</term>, or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” <note>A faint identifying image or text embedded in the digital file to show its origin.</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

These books belong to the public, and we act only as their caretakers. However, this work is very costly. To make sure we can keep providing this service, we have put some rules in place to prevent commercial companies from using these files unfairly, including technical limits on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using a computer program to automatically send many searches or requests to a system at once</term>.

This is a **digital copy** <term>digital copy: an electronic version of a physical book, created by scanning paper pages into a computer format for online reading</term> of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>copyright: a legal protection that gives creators exclusive rights to their work for a limited time</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: works that are no longer protected by copyright and are free for anyone to use, copy, or share</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <margin>marginalia: notes, stamps, or doodles written in the margins of a book by its previous owners or librarians</margin> present in the original volume will appear in this file - a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitization: the technical process of converting physical materials, like books and photos, into digital files</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, **optical character recognition** <note>OCR (Optical Character Recognition): technology that "reads" the text in a scanned image and converts it into a digital text file that can be searched or edited</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” <term>watermark: a faint logo or design placed on a digital page to identify the source of the file</term> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical paper or parchment into a digital format that can be viewed on screens</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using computer scripts or "bots" to automatically search or download data in bulk</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation**, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition (OCR): the electronic conversion of images of typed, handwritten, or printed text into machine-encoded text</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “**watermark**” <term>watermark: a faint identifying mark or logo placed on a digital file to identify its source</term> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the technical process of converting physical pages into digital images and searchable text</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: the use of automated scripts or "bots" to fetch data from a website without human intervention</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. This is a **digital copy** <term>digital copy: a modern electronic version of a physical book, created by capturing images of every page to make it readable on computers and devices</term> of a book that was kept for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google. This was done as part of a project to make the world’s books discoverable online.

The book has survived long enough for its **copyright** <term>copyright: a legal rule that gives the creator of a work the sole right to decide how it is used</term> to expire, and the book has entered the **public domain** <term>public domain: a status for creative works that are no longer owned by any one person or company, meaning they belong to everyone</term>. Whether a book is in the public domain can vary from country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture, and knowledge that is often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations, and other **marginalia** <note>original: "marginalia"; these are the small notes, stamps, or doodles left in the margins of a book by its previous owners or librarians over many decades</note> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

### Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical paper and ink into a digital format that can be stored and shared electronically</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public, and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system. If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>machine translation: the use of software to translate text from one language to another</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition (OCR): the technology used to turn images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text</term>, or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we cannot offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>copyright infringement: using someone else's copyrighted work without permission, which can lead to legal consequences</term> liability can be quite severe.

This is a digital copy of a book that was kept safe for many generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google. This is part of a large project to make the world’s books searchable and discoverable online.

The book has lasted long enough for its **copyright** <term>copyright: a legal right that gives the creator of a work control over its use and distribution</term> to expire, allowing it to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws and belong to the public rather than an individual creator</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has ended. Whether a book is in the public domain can change from one country to another. These books are windows into the past, offering a rich collection of history, culture, and knowledge that is often hard to find elsewhere.

You might see marks, stamps, or other **marginalia** <term>marginalia: handwritten notes, stamps, or marks made in the margins or pages of a book by previous owners or librarians</term> from the original physical volume. These are reminders of the book’s long journey from its first printing to a library and, eventually, to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to work with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting a physical object, like a book, into a digital image or text format for computer use</term> public domain materials to make them easy for everyone to access. These books belong to the public; we are simply their caretakers. However, because this work is expensive, we have set certain rules to prevent commercial abuse, including technical limits on automated searching.

We also ask that you:

*   *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for individuals. We request that you use these files only for your own personal, non-business purposes.

*   *Refrain from automated querying* Do not use software to send automatic searches to Google’s system. If you are a researcher working on **machine translation** <note>The use of software to translate text from one language to another.</note> or **optical character recognition** <note>Commonly known as OCR; the technology that turns images of text into searchable digital text.</note>, please contact us. We support the use of public domain materials for these goals and may be able to help.

*   *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" <note>A faint identifying image or text overlaid on a document to show its source.</note> you see on each file is necessary to let people know about this project and help them find more books. Please do not remove it.

*   *Keep it legal* You are responsible for making sure your use of this book follows the law. Just because a book is in the public domain in the United States does not mean it is free to use in other countries. Copyright laws vary by location, and we cannot provide legal advice. Do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used however you like anywhere in the world. The legal penalties for copyright infringement can be very serious.

This is a digital copy of a book that was preserved for generations on library shelves before it was carefully scanned by Google as part of a project to make the world's books discoverable online.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>copyright: a legal framework that gives the creator of a work exclusive rights to its use and distribution for a specific number of years</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: the state of works whose intellectual property rights have expired, making them free for anyone to use or share</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that's often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <term>marginalia: notes, scribbles, or comments written by previous readers in the margins of a book's pages</term> present in the original volume will appear in this file - a reminder of this book's long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical materials into a digital format, such as an image or an e-book</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using software programs or "bots" to search through data much faster than a human could</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ **Make non-commercial use of the files** We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ **Refrain from automated querying** Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>Original: OCR; the technology that recognizes text within images</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ **Maintain attribution** The Google "watermark" <note>A faint, identifying image or text placed over the digital file to show its origin</note> you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ **Keep it legal** Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

It has survived long enough for the **copyright** <term>copyright: a legal protection that gives the creator of a work the exclusive right to control how it is used and shared</term> to expire and the book to enter the **public domain** <term>public domain: creative works that are no longer protected by intellectual property laws and can be freely used by anyone</term>. A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. ## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical items, like paper books, into a digital format that can be viewed on a computer</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using a computer program to send many search requests very quickly, which can overwhelm a system</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, **non-commercial** <term>non-commercial: use that is intended for personal or educational benefit rather than for making money</term> purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>machine translation: using software to translate text from one language to another</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition (OCR): technology that recognizes text within digital images, turning a "picture" of a page into searchable text</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement** <term>copyright infringement: using a copyrighted work without the permission of the owner, which can lead to legal penalties</term> liability can be quite severe.

A public domain book is one that was never subject to copyright or whose legal copyright term has expired. Whether a book is in the public domain may vary country to country. Public domain books are our gateways to the past, representing a wealth of history, culture and knowledge that’s often difficult to discover.

Marks, notations and other **marginalia** <term>marginalia: notes, marks, or comments written in the margins of a text by previous owners or readers</term> present in the original volume will appear in this file—a reminder of this book’s long journey from the publisher to a library and finally to you.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to digitize public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using software programs to search a database automatically rather than a human doing it manually</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are conducting research on machine translation, optical character recognition or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain **attribution*** <term>attribution: the act of acknowledging the source or creator of a work</term> The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

## Usage guidelines

Google is proud to partner with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the process of converting physical text or images into a digital format that can be processed by a computer</term> public domain materials and make them widely accessible. Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on automated querying.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google’s system: If you are looking for research on machine translation, optical character recognition <note>original: OCR</note> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google “watermark” you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can’t offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book’s appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. Copyright infringement liability can be quite severe.

Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their custodians. Nevertheless, this work is expensive, so in order to keep providing this resource, we have taken steps to prevent abuse by commercial parties, including placing technical restrictions on **automated querying** <term>automated querying: using computer programs to automatically search or download large amounts of data at high speeds</term>.

We also ask that you:

+ *Make non-commercial use of the files* We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.

+ *Refrain from automated querying* Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system: If you are conducting research on **machine translation** <term>machine translation: using software to translate text from one language to another</term>, **optical character recognition** <term>optical character recognition: technology that converts images of typed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text</term> or other areas where access to a large amount of text is helpful, please contact us. We encourage the use of public domain materials for these purposes and may be able to help.

+ *Maintain attribution* The Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.

+ *Keep it legal* Whatever your use, remember that you are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal. Do not assume that just because we believe a book is in the public domain for users in the United States, that the work is also in the public domain for users in other countries. Whether a book is still in copyright varies from country to country, and we can't offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed. Please do not assume that a book's appearance in Google Book Search means it can be used in any manner anywhere in the world. **Copyright infringement liability** <note>This refers to the legal and financial responsibility one faces for using copyrighted material without permission.</note> can be quite severe.

Google is proud to work with libraries to **digitize** <term>digitize: the conversion of physical materials into digital information so they can be viewed on a computer</term> public domain materials and make them available to everyone.
